text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kenya's soccer "Dream Team" Harambee Stars stuns Nigeria soccer giants Super Eagles when they hold them to a 1-1 draw in a World Cup qualifier at the Moi International Sports Centre in Nairobi.

- Anglican Archbishop David Gitari ascends to the leadership of the Church of the Province of Kenya with a dramatic call for the postponement of the General Election and an urgent review of the country's constitution.
- Leading opposition politician Paul Muite and other activists of the unregistered Safina party escape a police dragnet near the central province town of Nyeri.
- Dr David Gitari is enthroned as Archbishop and head of the (Anglican) Church of the Province of Kenya.
- One man is taken to hospital unconscious and several others injured during elections of interim officials of the opposition National Development party of Kenya in Mombasa.
- A group of ethnic Kikuyu politicians plans to revive the defunct pre-independence Kikuyu Central Association so as to unite the Kikuyu community in Kenya.
- Main opposition FORD-Kenya party Mombasa branch office says the invasion and take-over of their offices by the National Development Party of Kenya is illegal.
- Assistant Minister for Public Works and Housing Kassim Mwamzandi confirms that he has floated shares worth 20 million shillings of the moribund Ramisi Sugar Factory.

- The search for the Kenyan fugitive implicated in the theft of 54 million shillings ($1 million) belonging to Citibank N.A. takes on a regional dimension following confirmation from police in Tanzania that they have joined the hunt for the suspect.
- Uganda's Leadership Code of Conduct takes off with public figures from the president to primary school heads being asked to declare their wealth by January 31.
- The Tanzanian government is to throw out its six-year-old investment Act and introduce new legislation to lure foreign entrepreneurs.
